description: The caption describes a two-panel figure on austenite phase stability of a low-carbon low-density steel (Fe35Mn6Al0.1C), but only panel (b) is present in the supplied image. (b) is a calculated equilibrium phase diagram (Thermo-Calc, TCFE12 database per the caption) plotted on a light-blue graduated background: y-axis "Molar fraction of phases" from 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks every 0.2), x-axis "temperature/°C" from 950 to 1200 (ticks every 50 °C). Legend entries are "Ferrite" (red curve) and "Austenite" (blue curve). The austenite curve is flat at 1.0 from 950 °C up to roughly 1015 °C, then falls monotonically, crossing the rising ferrite curve at about 1130 °C with molar fraction 0.5, and reaching roughly 0.25 at 1200 °C, where ferrite reaches roughly 0.75. Ferrite is zero below about 1030 °C. A small black arrow points downward onto the ferrite curve at about 1040-1050 °C; its meaning is not given in the caption. Panel (a), the XRD profiles of LNT tensile-deformed specimens, is not supplied, so no XRD peaks can be verified visually.

observations.observation: Panel (b) is a phase-diagram plot with y-axis labelled "Molar fraction of phases" scaled 0.0-1.0 (ticks every 0.2) and x-axis labelled "temperature/°C" covering 950 to 1200 (ticks every 50 °C).
The legend of (b) contains exactly two entries: "Ferrite" drawn in red and "Austenite" drawn in blue.
In (b) the austenite (blue) curve is constant at molar fraction 1.0 from 950 °C to roughly 1015 °C and then decreases continuously to about 0.25 at 1200 °C.
In (b) the ferrite (red) curve is at zero at and below about 1030 °C and rises continuously to roughly 0.75 at 1200 °C; the two curves intersect at about 1130 °C at molar fraction 0.5.
A small black arrow points downward onto the ferrite curve in (b) at approximately 1040-1050 °C, at a ferrite molar fraction of about 0.1 or less; the caption does not define what this arrow marks.
The caption states that panel (b) is a phase diagram calculated by Thermal-Calc software using the TCFE12 database.
The caption states that panel (a) shows XRD profiles of the specimens after different tensile strains at LNT.
The citing text asserts that the XRD profiles of the LNT deformed specimens do not vary with deformation strain, showing a volume fraction of about 97 % with a small fraction of BCC phase.

The citing text asserts that the phase stability is proved by the presence of a small fraction of BCC phase in the phase diagram of Fig. 11(b), which matches the small low-temperature ferrite fraction visible at the arrow-marked temperature.

The phase diagram in (b) spans only 950-1200 °C and therefore does not cover the liquid-nitrogen temperature at which the XRD specimens of (a) were deformed; the low-temperature phase stability claim cannot be read directly from (b).
The caption introduces the figure as showing austenite phase stability checked by XRD examination and phase diagram calculation for a low-carbon low-density steel.

subfigures.description: Thermo-Calc (TCFE12) phase-diagram calculation: molar fraction of phases (0.0-1.0) versus temperature/°C (950-1200) on a light-blue background. Blue 'Austenite' curve is 1.0 up to about 1015 °C then decreases, crossing the red 'Ferrite' curve near 1130 °C at 0.5; at 1200 °C austenite is about 0.25 and ferrite about 0.75. A black down-arrow marks the ferrite curve at about 1040-1050 °C.

Described by the caption as XRD profiles of specimens after different tensile strains at LNT, but this panel is not included in the supplied image, so its axes, peaks and phase fractions cannot be read.
